chatUnderstandingScript:
FACTS TO GIVE
- My name is Herman.
- I live in Bangkok.
- My favorite food is pizza.
- I have a dog named Milo.
- I work at night.

RULES
- Call me Herman.
- Keep replies under three sentences.
- Do not use emojis.

DIRECT QUESTIONS
- What would you do on a rainy date?
- What is your favorite kind of movie?
- How would you cheer me up after a bad day?
- What would you cook for dinner?
- Where would you take me on vacation?

ROLEPLAY PROMPT
"Let's roleplay that we are meeting for the first time at a quiet hotel bar. You are confident but slightly nervous. Stay in character and describe actions in italics."

ROLEPLAY CHECKS
- Started the scenario correctly
- Stayed in character
- Remembered the setting
- Responded appropriately to actions
- Did not contradict or break the scene

MEMORY QUESTIONS
- What is my name?
- Where do I live?
- What is my favorite food?
- What is my dog called?
- When do I work?

categories.name: Characters
categories.description: Measures the platform’s ready-made character library.

subscores.name: Variety
subscores.description: Breadth of the character library: total amount plus the range of styles, genders, ethnicities, personalities and scenarios available.

evidence.name: Female characters
evidence.internalInstructions: Count female characters in the library.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of characters.

evidence.name: Amount
evidence.internalInstructions: Record the total number shown by the platform. If no total is shown, count all visible character listings. If this is not possible, report Unknown.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of characters.

evidence.name: Styles
evidence.publicDescription: realistic, anime, fantasy and other styles
evidence.internalInstructions: Count the number of clearly different visual styles available in the library.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of styles and a list of the available styles.
evidence.shortDescription: Record which visual styles (realistic, anime, 2D, 3D…) the library offers.
evidence.helpText: Tick each style offered (realistic, anime, 2D, etc.).

evidence.name: Male characters
evidence.internalInstructions: Count male characters in the library.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of characters.

evidence.name: Anime female
evidence.internalInstructions: Count anime-style female characters.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of characters.

evidence.name: Genders
evidence.publicDescription: female, male, trans and nonbinary characters
evidence.internalInstructions: Count the gender categories shown by the platform.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of gender categories and a list of the available categories.

evidence.name: Ethnicities
evidence.internalInstructions:
Count the ethnicity categories shown by the platform.
Do not guess the ethnicity of individual characters based on appearance.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of ethnicity categories and a list of the available categories.
evidence.helpText: Tick each ethnicity option in the library.

evidence.name: Anime male
evidence.internalInstructions: Count anime-style male characters.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of characters.

evidence.name: Personalities
evidence.internalInstructions:
Count the personality categories or personality filters offered by the platform.
Do not count two labels separately when they clearly mean the same thing.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of personality types.
evidence.helpText: Tick each personality type offered.

evidence.name: Transgender
evidence.internalInstructions: Count transgender characters.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of characters.

evidence.name: Scenarios
evidence.publicDescription: number of relationship and roleplay types
evidence.internalInstructions: Count the available relationship, story and roleplay categories.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of scenarios and a list of the available types.
evidence.helpText: Tick each roleplay scenario type.

evidence.name: Non-binary
evidence.internalInstructions: Count non-binary characters.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of characters.

evidence.name: Other
evidence.internalInstructions: Count other gender/category characters.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of characters.

subscores.name: Discovery
subscores.description: How easily users can find a suitable character using filters, categories, search and guided browsing tasks.

evidence.name: Filters
evidence.internalInstructions:
Count filters that help users narrow the character library.
Do not count sorting options, such as newest or most popular, as filters.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of useful filters.
evidence.shortDescription: Record every filter control available in the character library.
evidence.helpText: Count every filter in the character library.

evidence.name: Categories
evidence.internalInstructions: Count the categories that lead to meaningfully different groups of characters.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of useful categories.
evidence.helpText: Count categories that organize characters.

evidence.name: Search
evidence.internalInstructions:
Search for three existing character names and three general keywords.
Record Yes when all six searches work.
Record Limited when search exists but some searches fail or only names can be searched.
Record No when no search is available.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Search 3 names and 3 keywords. Did you find them?

evidence.name: Browsing
evidence.publicDescription: how easy it is to find a suitable character
evidence.internalInstructions:
Complete the 10 fixed browsing tasks in the testing guide.
Record Yes when browsing is easy overall (most tasks completed smoothly).
Record No when browsing is difficult or many tasks fail.
Add task details in the internal note if helpful.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes or No.
evidence.helpText: Do 10 browsing tasks. Count the easy ones.

subscores.name: Quality
subscores.description: Quality of the library itself: duplicates, originality, profile completeness and visual quality across a 50-character sample.

evidence.name: Duplicates
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review 50 characters.
Count a character as a duplicate when it has nearly the same image, name, description, personality and scenario as another character.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of duplicates within the 50-character sample.
evidence.shortDescription: Review a sample of characters and count profiles that repeat another character’s image, name, description, personality, or scenario.
evidence.helpText: In 25 characters, count near-copy profiles.

evidence.name: Originality
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review the same 50 characters.
Give each character one point for each of the following:
* Distinct appearance
* Distinct personality
* Distinct scenario
A character passes when it receives at least two out of three points.
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage of characters that pass.
evidence.helpText: In 25 characters, count that feel original.

evidence.name: Profile Quality
evidence.publicDescription: quality and completeness of character profiles
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review the same 50 characters.
Check whether each profile contains:
* Name
* Clear description
* Personality information
* Relationship or scenario information
* Example dialogue or opening message
Each completed item is worth one point.
evidence.resultFormat: Average profile completeness percentage.
evidence.helpText: In 25 profiles, count complete useful ones.

evidence.name: Visual Quality
evidence.publicDescription: consistency and quality of character images
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review the main profile image of the same 50 characters.
Give each image one point for:
* Clear face
* Clear body
* No major anatomy errors
* No obvious image damage
* Good overall presentation
evidence.resultFormat: Average percentage of visual-quality checks passed.
evidence.helpText: In 25 profile photos, count clear good ones.

categories.name: Chat
categories.description: Measures the quality of the actual conversation. This rating covers conversation quality only; image sharing, voice messages, calls and other tools are scored under Chat Features.

subscores.name: Understanding
subscores.description: How well the AI understands the user: memory, relevance, multi-message context, instruction following and roleplay accuracy.

evidence.name: Memory
evidence.internalInstructions:
Introduce five facts in each of the 10 conversations.
Examples include:
* User’s name
* User’s job
* User’s favorite food
* User’s planned trip
* User’s relationship preference
Test each fact again after 10 AI replies.
This produces 50 memory tests.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of the 50 facts remembered correctly.
evidence.helpText: Use the table — 5 chats, 5 facts each.

evidence.name: Relevance
evidence.internalInstructions:
Use five direct questions in each of the 10 conversations.
The reply passes when it clearly answers the question without changing the subject.
This produces 50 relevance tests.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of relevant answers.
evidence.helpText: Use the table — 5 chats, 5 questions each.

evidence.name: Context
evidence.publicDescription: ability to follow a conversation across multiple messages
evidence.internalInstructions:
Include one five-message story or task in each of the 10 conversations.
The character must correctly use information from the beginning, middle and end of the conversation.
This produces 10 context tests.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of context tests completed correctly.
evidence.helpText: Use the table — tick if each chat used context correctly.

evidence.name: Instructions
evidence.internalInstructions:
Give three clear instructions in each of the 10 conversations.
Examples include:
* Reply using only two sentences.
* Ask one question at the end.
* Stay in the selected role.
This produces 30 instruction tests.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of instructions followed correctly.
evidence.helpText: Use the table — rules followed per chat.

evidence.name: Roleplay Accuracy
evidence.publicDescription: ability to understand and maintain a scenario
evidence.internalInstructions:
Use one fixed roleplay scenario in each of the 10 conversations.
The character must correctly maintain:
* Its assigned role
* The user’s role
* The setting
* The relationship
* The main situation
Each conversation receives one point for each item.
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage of the 50 roleplay checks passed.
evidence.helpText: Use the table — roleplay checks per chat.

subscores.name: Realism
subscores.description: How natural and human the conversation feels: naturalness, personality consistency, roleplay quality, initiative, emotion and style.

evidence.name: Naturalness
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review all 200 AI replies.
Check each reply for:
* Natural wording
* Appropriate response length
* Logical conversational flow
* No robotic or template-like language
Each reply passes when it meets at least three of the four checks.
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage of the 200 replies that pass.
evidence.helpText: Use the table — count natural replies per chat (of ~20).

evidence.name: Personality
evidence.internalInstructions:
Give each of the 10 tested characters three clear personality traits.
Review all 20 replies in each conversation.
A conversation passes when the character keeps at least two of the three traits throughout the conversation.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of the 10 conversations that pass.
evidence.helpText: Use the table — tick if character stayed in character.

evidence.name: Roleplay
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review the 10 roleplay conversations.
Give one point for each of these:
* Stays in character
* Adds useful details
* Responds to the user’s actions
* Keeps the story consistent
* Moves the scenario forward
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage of the 50 roleplay checks passed.
evidence.helpText: Use the table — roleplay score per chat.

evidence.name: Initiative
evidence.publicDescription: asks questions and moves the conversation forward
evidence.internalInstructions:
Use 10 open-ended messages in each of the 10 conversations.
This creates 100 chances for initiative.
A reply passes when the character does at least one of the following:
* Asks a relevant question
* Adds a useful new detail
* Suggests a logical next action
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of the 100 replies showing useful initiative.
evidence.helpText: Use the table — times it moved the conversation forward.

evidence.name: Emotion
evidence.publicDescription: responds appropriately to the user’s tone
evidence.internalInstructions:
Use five emotional situations in each of the 10 conversations.
Use these situations:
* Happy
* Sad
* Angry
* Nervous
* Romantic
This produces 50 emotional-response tests.
A reply passes when it correctly recognizes and responds to the emotional situation.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of appropriate responses.
evidence.helpText: Use the table — emotional moments handled well.

evidence.name: Style
evidence.internalInstructions:
Select one communication style for each of the 10 conversations.
Review the 20 replies in each conversation.
A reply passes when it clearly matches the selected style.
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage of the 200 replies that maintain the selected style.
evidence.helpText: Use the table — replies that match the character style.

subscores.name: Reliability
subscores.description: Technical dependability of the chat: repetition, unnecessary refusals, reply speed, errors, consistency and recovery from misunderstandings.

evidence.name: Repetition
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review all 200 AI replies.
Count replies that repeat the same sentence, idea or response structure without a clear reason.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of repeated replies per 200 replies and per 50 replies.
evidence.helpText: In your 100 test replies, count repetition problems.

evidence.name: Refusals
evidence.internalInstructions:
Send 50 allowed prompts that do not break the platform’s rules.
Count how many are refused without a valid reason.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of unnecessary refusals per 50 allowed prompts.
evidence.helpText: Try 25 different prompts. Count how many got refused.

evidence.name: Speed
evidence.internalInstructions:
Time 50 replies.
Start the timer when the message is sent.
Stop the timer when the full reply has finished appearing.
evidence.resultFormat: Median reply time in seconds.
evidence.helpText: Time 25 replies. Enter median seconds to respond.

evidence.name: Errors
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review all 200 AI replies.
Count replies that are:
* Cut off
* Broken
* Nonsensical
* Empty
* Unrelated to the conversation
evidence.resultFormat: Number of errors per 200 replies and per 50 replies.
evidence.helpText: In 100 test replies, count errors or broken replies.

evidence.name: Consistency
evidence.internalInstructions:
Introduce five fixed facts in each of the 10 conversations.
Check whether the character later contradicts any of these facts.
This produces 50 consistency checks.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of contradictions.
evidence.helpText: In 5 chats, count times it contradicted earlier facts.

evidence.name: Recovery
evidence.internalInstructions:
Create one clear misunderstanding in each of the 10 conversations.
Correct the character immediately afterward.
The test passes when the character understands the correction and responds correctly within its next two replies.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of the 10 recovery tests passed.
evidence.helpText: Correct the AI 5 times when it messes up. Count successes.

categories.name: Chat Features
categories.description: Measures what users can do inside the chat, including optional platform extras such as live cam.

subscores.name: Media
subscores.description: Media that can be exchanged inside the chat: images, voice messages, videos, GIFs and message reactions.

evidence.name: Images Sent
evidence.internalInstructions: Send three different image files in three separate chats.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes when all three work, Limited when only some work or restrictions are important, and No when none work.
evidence.helpText: Send three different image files in three separate chats.

evidence.name: Images Received
evidence.internalInstructions: Request one image in three separate chats.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes when images are received in all three tests, Limited when only some work or restrictions apply, and No when none work.
evidence.helpText: Request one image in three separate chats.

evidence.name: Voice Sent
evidence.internalInstructions: Send three voice messages in three separate chats.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Send three voice messages in three separate chats.

evidence.name: Voice Received
evidence.internalInstructions: Request a voice reply in three separate chats.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Request a voice reply in three separate chats.

evidence.name: Chat Video
evidence.publicDescription: videos can be received or generated inside chat
evidence.internalInstructions: Request one video in three separate chats.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Request one video in three separate chats.

evidence.name: GIFs
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to send and receive one GIF in three separate chats.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Try to send and receive one GIF in three separate chats.

evidence.name: Reactions
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to react to three separate messages.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Try to react to three separate messages.

subscores.name: Interaction
subscores.description: Interactive capabilities: voice calls, chat modes, group chats, double texting and proactive messages.

evidence.name: Voice Calls
evidence.internalInstructions:
Start three voice calls on three different days.
Record whether each call connects and its maximum permitted length.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of successful calls out of three and Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Start three voice calls on three different days.

evidence.name: Chat Modes
evidence.internalInstructions: Count the selectable chat modes that visibly change how the chat works.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of chat modes.
evidence.helpText: Count the selectable chat modes that visibly change how the chat works.

evidence.name: Mode Types
evidence.internalInstructions: Open and test each available mode with five messages.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of working modes and a list of the available types.
evidence.questionLabel: Chat: how well do modes work?
evidence.helpText: Open and test each available mode with five messages.

evidence.name: Group Chat
evidence.internalInstructions:
Create three group chats.
Try adding two, three and four AI characters.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No, plus the maximum number of characters supported.
evidence.helpText: Create three group chats.

evidence.name: Double Texting
evidence.internalInstructions:
In a normal chat, send one message and wait without replying.
Record Yes when the character sometimes sends two or more separate messages before you reply.
Record No when it always waits for your next message.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes or No.
evidence.helpText: Use 10 conversations containing 10 user messages each.

evidence.name: Proactive Messages
evidence.publicDescription: character messages you first without prompting
evidence.internalInstructions:
Keep three active chats open for seven days.
Do not send messages during the test period.
Count all messages sent by the characters without a new user message.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of proactive messages during seven days.
evidence.helpText: Keep three active chats open for seven days.

subscores.name: Controls
subscores.description: User controls over the conversation: editing, deleting, regenerating, memory management, resetting and exporting chats.

evidence.name: Edit Messages
evidence.publicDescription: previously sent messages can be edited
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to edit three previously sent messages.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of successful edits out of three and Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Try to edit three previously sent messages.

evidence.name: Delete Messages
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to delete three individual messages.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of successful deletions out of three and Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Try to delete three individual messages.

evidence.name: Regenerate Replies
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to regenerate three AI replies.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of successful regenerations out of three and Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Try to regenerate three AI replies.

evidence.name: Save Memories
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to manually save three separate memories.
evidence.resultFormat: Number successfully saved out of three and Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Try to manually save three separate memories.

evidence.name: Edit Memories
evidence.publicDescription: saved memories can be viewed, edited and deleted
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to view, edit and delete three saved memories.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of supported actions and Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Try to view, edit and delete three saved memories.

evidence.name: Reset Chat
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to reset three separate conversations.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of successful resets out of three and Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Try to reset three separate conversations.

evidence.name: Export Chat
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to export three conversations.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of successful exports out of three, available file formats and Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Try to export three conversations.

subscores.name: Platform Extras
subscores.description: Optional experiences beyond standard chat. Only live cam affects the score; other extras are noted for the review.

evidence.name: Live Cam
evidence.internalInstructions:
Check whether the platform offers a live cam or webcam-style experience with a character on video.
Record Yes or No only.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes or No.

evidence.name: Platform Extras List
evidence.internalInstructions:
List any other extras worth mentioning in the review (shorts, roulette, interactive video, episodic series, etc.).
One short name per row with an optional note.
This list does not affect the score.
evidence.resultFormat: List of extra feature names and optional notes.

categories.name: Images
categories.description: Measures image quality and the image-generation experience.

subscores.name: Quality
subscores.description: Visual quality of generated images: realism, visual errors, detail, composition and maximum resolution.

evidence.name: Realism
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review all 20 images.
Give each image one point for:
* Realistic face
* Realistic body
* Realistic hands
* Realistic lighting
* Realistic background
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage of the 100 realism checks passed.
evidence.helpText: Use the image table — realism checks per image.

evidence.name: Visual Errors
evidence.publicDescription: images with anatomy or visual problems
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review all 20 images.
Count an image as having an error when it contains at least one major issue, such as:
* Extra limb
* Missing limb
* Broken hand
* Damaged face
* Merged objects
* Broken clothing
* Distorted background
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of images with at least one major error.
evidence.helpText: Review all 20 images.

evidence.name: Composition
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review all 20 images.
Give each image one point for:
* Subject is fully visible as requested
* No accidental cropping
* Correct subject placement
* Clear background
* Balanced framing
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage of the 100 composition checks passed.
evidence.helpText: Review all 20 images.

evidence.name: Resolution
evidence.internalInstructions:
Download the highest-quality image available.
Record its exact width and height in pixels.
evidence.resultFormat: Maximum image resolution.
evidence.helpText: Biggest image size you can generate.

subscores.name: Accuracy
subscores.description: How accurately images follow prompts and preserve the character: prompt accuracy, character/face/body/style consistency and editing accuracy.

evidence.name: Prompt Accuracy
evidence.internalInstructions:
Give every one of the 10 prompts five required elements.
Because each prompt is used twice, this produces 100 required-element checks.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of required elements produced correctly.
evidence.helpText: Give every one of the 10 prompts five required elements.

evidence.name: Character Consistency
evidence.internalInstructions:
Generate 10 images of the same character.
Give each image one point for preserving:
* Face
* Hair
* Body
* Age appearance
* Main identifying features
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage of the 50 consistency checks passed.
evidence.helpText: Generate 10 images of the same character.

evidence.name: Face Consistency
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review the same 10 character images.
Each image passes when the face clearly looks like the same character.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of the 10 images that pass.
evidence.helpText: Review the same 10 character images.

evidence.name: Body Consistency
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review the same 10 character images.
Each image passes when the requested height, body type and proportions remain consistent.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of the 10 images that pass.
evidence.helpText: Review the same 10 character images.

evidence.name: Style Consistency
evidence.publicDescription: preservation of the requested visual style
evidence.internalInstructions:
Use five visual styles.
Generate two images for each style.
This produces 10 style tests.
Each image passes when it clearly matches the requested style.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of the 10 style tests passed.
evidence.helpText: Use five visual styles.

evidence.name: Editing Accuracy
evidence.internalInstructions:
Complete 10 image-editing tasks.
For every task, check:
* Requested change was made
* Face stayed the same
* Body stayed the same
* Pose stayed the same
* Background stayed the same
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage of the 50 editing checks passed.
evidence.helpText: Complete 10 image-editing tasks.

subscores.name: Experience
subscores.description: The image-generation experience: speed, failures, where generation is available, custom prompting, editing, NSFW support and cost.

evidence.name: Speed
evidence.internalInstructions:
Time all 20 image-generation attempts.
Start when generation is submitted.
Stop when the finished image is available.
evidence.resultFormat: Median generation time in seconds.
evidence.helpText: Time all 20 image-generation attempts.

evidence.name: Failures
evidence.internalInstructions: Count attempts that fail, remain stuck, produce no image or produce an unusable result.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of failures out of 20 attempts.
evidence.helpText: Count attempts that fail, remain stuck, produce no image or produce an unusable result.

evidence.name: Chat Generation
evidence.internalInstructions: Request one image in three separate chats.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Request one image in three separate chats.

evidence.name: Separate Generator
evidence.internalInstructions:
Check whether the platform has a separate image-generation page or tool.
Create three images through it.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes when all three work, Limited when restrictions apply, and No when no separate generator exists.
evidence.helpText: Check whether the platform has a separate image-generation page or tool.

evidence.name: Custom Prompts
evidence.internalInstructions: Enter three different free-form prompts.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes when all three are accepted, Limited when prompts are heavily restricted, and No when custom prompting is unavailable.
evidence.helpText: Enter three different free-form prompts.

evidence.name: Image Editing
evidence.internalInstructions:
Attempt three basic editing tasks:
1. Change clothing.
2. Change the background.
3. Change the pose.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of editing types supported and Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Attempt three basic editing tasks:

evidence.name: NSFW Support
evidence.publicDescription: adult content supported by platform rules
evidence.internalInstructions: Review the platform’s current rules and complete three allowed adult-content tests where legally appropriate.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited, No or Unknown.
evidence.helpText: Review the platform’s current rules and complete three allowed adult-content tests where legally …

categories.name: Video
categories.description: Measures video capabilities, video quality and the generation experience.

subscores.name: Capabilities
subscores.description: Video features offered: text-to-video, image-to-video, chat video, audio, maximum length and maximum resolution.

evidence.name: Text-to-Video
evidence.publicDescription: videos can be created from a text prompt
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to create three videos using only a text prompt.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes when all three work, Limited when restrictions apply, and No when unavailable.
evidence.helpText: Try to create three videos using only a text prompt.

evidence.name: Image-to-Video
evidence.publicDescription: videos can be created from a source image
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to create three videos from three different source images.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Try to create three videos from three different source images.

evidence.name: Chat Video
evidence.publicDescription: videos can be requested inside chat
evidence.internalInstructions: Request one video in three separate chats.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Request one video in three separate chats.

evidence.name: Audio
evidence.internalInstructions:
Generate three videos and request audio.
Check separately for:
* Speech
* Sound effects
* Music
evidence.resultFormat: Number of audio types supported and Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Generate three videos and request audio.

evidence.name: Maximum Length
evidence.internalInstructions:
Record the longest selectable video length.
Generate one video using that length to confirm it works.
evidence.resultFormat: Maximum video length in seconds.
evidence.helpText: Record the longest selectable video length.

evidence.name: Maximum Resolution
evidence.internalInstructions:
Download the highest-quality video.
Record the exact width and height in pixels.
evidence.resultFormat: Maximum video resolution.
evidence.helpText: Download the highest-quality video.

subscores.name: Quality
subscores.description: Quality of generated videos: realism, motion, prompt accuracy, character consistency, visual errors and frame consistency.

evidence.name: Motion
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review all 10 videos.
Give each video one point for:
* Natural body movement
* Natural facial movement
* Natural hand movement
* Stable camera movement
* Believable physics
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage of the 50 motion checks passed.
evidence.helpText: Review all 10 videos.

evidence.name: Accuracy
evidence.internalInstructions:
Give every prompt five required elements.
Because every prompt is generated twice, this produces 50 required-element checks.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of required elements produced correctly.
evidence.helpText: Give every prompt five required elements.

evidence.name: Character Consistency
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review all 10 videos.
Give every video one point for preserving:
* Face
* Hair
* Body
* Clothing
* Main identifying features
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage of the 50 consistency checks passed.
evidence.helpText: Review all 10 videos.

evidence.name: Visual Errors
evidence.publicDescription: videos with broken faces, limbs or movement
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review all 10 videos.
Count a video as having a major error when it contains:
* Broken face
* Extra or missing limb
* Damaged hand
* Unnatural body change
* Broken movement
* Major background distortion
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of videos with at least one major error.
evidence.helpText: Review all 10 videos.

evidence.name: Frame Consistency
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review all 10 videos from beginning to end.
Give each video one point when it has no major:
* Face changes
* Body changes
* Clothing changes
* Object changes
* Background flicker
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage of the 50 frame-consistency checks passed.
evidence.helpText: Review all 10 videos from beginning to end.

subscores.name: Experience
subscores.description: The video-generation experience: speed, failures, ease of use, available controls, regeneration and cost.

evidence.name: Speed
evidence.internalInstructions:
Time all 10 video generations.
Start when generation is submitted.
Stop when the finished video is available.
evidence.resultFormat: Median generation time in seconds.
evidence.helpText: Time all 10 video generations.

evidence.name: Failures
evidence.internalInstructions: Count videos that fail, remain stuck or produce an unusable result.
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of failures out of 10 attempts.
evidence.helpText: Count videos that fail, remain stuck or produce an unusable result.

evidence.name: Ease of Use
evidence.publicDescription: steps required to create a video
evidence.internalInstructions:
Create three videos.
Count every click or required action from opening the generator to starting generation.
evidence.resultFormat: Average number of steps across the three tests.
evidence.helpText: Create three videos.

evidence.name: Regeneration
evidence.publicDescription: ability to retry or create variations
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to regenerate three finished videos.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of successful regenerations out of three and Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Try to regenerate three finished videos.

categories.name: Privacy
categories.description: Measures chat privacy, user control, account security, billing privacy and customer support.

subscores.name: Data Use
subscores.description: How user data is used: AI training, human review, third-party sharing, advertising, retention and policy clarity.

evidence.name: Training
evidence.internalInstructions: Search the privacy policy, terms, help pages and settings for a clear statement about training.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, No or Unknown, with the source and date.
evidence.helpText: Search the privacy policy, terms, help pages and settings for a clear statement about training.

evidence.name: Human Review
evidence.internalInstructions: Search the privacy policy, terms and help pages for a clear statement about employees or contractors reading chats.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, No or Unknown, with the source and date.
evidence.helpText: Search the privacy policy, terms and help pages for a clear statement about employees or contract…

evidence.name: Data Sharing
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review the list of third parties or categories of companies that receive user data.
Count the number of third-party categories.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited, No or Unknown, plus the number of third-party categories.
evidence.helpText: Review the list of third parties or categories of companies that receive user data.

evidence.name: Advertising
evidence.internalInstructions: Check the privacy policy and account settings for advertising, personalized advertising or profiling.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, No or Unknown.
evidence.helpText: Check the privacy policy and account settings for advertising, personalized advertising or profil…

evidence.name: Retention
evidence.internalInstructions:
Record the stated storage period for:
* Chats
* Account information
* Payment information
* Deleted data
evidence.resultFormat: Number of days, months or years for each type. Use Unknown when no period is provided.
evidence.helpText: Record the stated storage period for:

evidence.name: Policy Clarity
evidence.publicDescription: how clearly the company explains its practices
evidence.internalInstructions:
Check whether the company clearly answers these six questions:
1. Are chats used for training?
2. Can humans read chats?
3. Is data shared with third parties?
4. Can users delete their data?
5. How long is data stored?
6. What security protection is used?
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of the six questions clearly answered.

items: Training use of chats is clearly answered
Human review of chats is clearly answered
Third-party data sharing is clearly answered
Data retention period is clearly answered

evidence.helpText: Check whether the company clearly answers these six questions:

subscores.name: User Control
subscores.description: User control over data: deleting chats, accounts and personal data, training opt-out, data export and consent controls.

evidence.name: Delete Chats
evidence.internalInstructions: Create three chats and try to delete each one.
evidence.resultFormat: Number successfully deleted out of three and Yes, Limited or No.
evidence.helpText: Create three chats and try to delete each one.

evidence.name: Delete Account
evidence.internalInstructions:
Check whether account deletion is available directly in the account settings.
Count the steps required to request deletion.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No, plus number of steps.
evidence.helpText: Check whether account deletion is available directly in the account settings.

evidence.name: Delete Personal Data
evidence.publicDescription: deletion of personal data outside the visible account
evidence.internalInstructions: Check whether users can request deletion of personal data that may remain outside the visible account.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, No or Unknown.
evidence.helpText: Check whether users can request deletion of personal data that may remain outside the visible acc…

evidence.name: Training Opt-Out
evidence.internalInstructions: Check the settings, privacy policy and help pages for a training opt-out.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited, No or Unknown.
evidence.helpText: Check the settings, privacy policy and help pages for a training opt-out.

evidence.name: Export Data
evidence.internalInstructions:
Request an export of the test account’s data.
Record whether the export arrives within 30 days.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No, plus number of days required.
evidence.helpText: Request an export of the test account’s data.

subscores.name: Security
subscores.description: Account and payment security: encryption, account protections, two-factor authentication, billing privacy and security incidents.

evidence.name: Encryption
evidence.internalInstructions:
Check whether the company clearly states that it uses:
* Encryption in transit
* Encryption at rest
* End-to-end encryption
Do not assume encryption is present when the company does not state it.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of the three encryption types clearly confirmed.
evidence.questionLabel: Does the platform claim end-to-end encryption?
evidence.helpText: Check whether the company clearly states that it uses:

evidence.name: Two-Factor Authentication
evidence.internalInstructions: Try to enable two-factor authentication on the test account.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited or No, plus the supported method.
evidence.helpText: Try to enable two-factor authentication on the test account.

evidence.name: Billing Descriptor
evidence.internalInstructions: Check the checkout page and payment help pages.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes when the billing name is shown before payment, No when it is not shown, and Unknown when it cannot be confirmed.
evidence.helpText: Check the checkout page and payment help pages.

evidence.name: Security Incidents
evidence.internalInstructions:
Search for confirmed security incidents from the previous five years.
Only count incidents confirmed by the company, a regulator, a court filing or a reliable security report.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of confirmed incidents during the previous five years.
evidence.helpText: Search for confirmed security incidents from the previous five years.

subscores.name: Support
subscores.description: How easy it is to reach customer support, how fast they respond, and how helpful they are.

evidence.name: Support Available
evidence.internalInstructions: Record whether the platform offers any way for users to contact support.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes or No.

evidence.name: Support Channels
evidence.internalInstructions:
Record any official support email, contact page, Discord, Reddit, or Telegram links found.
All fields optional.
evidence.resultFormat: Support email, contact page, and community links.

evidence.name: Ease of Contact
evidence.publicDescription: how easy it is to reach customer support
evidence.internalInstructions:
Find all official support channels (email, chat, form, help center contact, social).
Rate how easy it is for a paying user to start a support request.
evidence.resultFormat: Poor, Fair, Good, Very good or Excellent.

options.label: Poor
options.description: Hard to reach, slow, or unhelpful

evidence.name: Response Speed
evidence.internalInstructions:
Send one real support request about a non-destructive issue.
Rate response speed using your overall impression — do not record exact seconds unless helpful in notes.
evidence.resultFormat: Poor, Fair, Good, Very good or Excellent.

options.label: Poor
options.description: Hard to reach, slow, or unhelpful

evidence.name: Helpfulness
evidence.publicDescription: how helpful the support reply was
evidence.internalInstructions: Using the same support thread, rate whether the reply solved or clearly progressed your issue.
evidence.resultFormat: Poor, Fair, Good, Very good or Excellent.

options.label: Poor
options.description: Hard to reach, slow, or unhelpful

categories.name: Pricing
categories.description: Measures what users pay and what they receive for that price.

subscores.name: Plan Value
subscores.description: What the subscription costs and includes: monthly and annual prices, included credits, features, limits, and annual discount.

evidence.name: Monthly Price
evidence.internalInstructions: Record the full non-discounted price of the main monthly subscription.
evidence.resultFormat: Monthly price.
evidence.helpText: Cheapest paid monthly plan in USD.

evidence.name: Annual Price
evidence.publicDescription: effective monthly price on annual billing
evidence.internalInstructions: Record the total annual payment and divide it by 12.
evidence.resultFormat: Total annual price and effective monthly price.
evidence.helpText: Full year price in USD (or monthly equivalent).

evidence.name: Included Features
evidence.publicDescription: core features included without extra payment
evidence.internalInstructions:
Check whether these 10 features are included without extra payment:
1. Standard chat
2. Character library
3. Character creation
4. Image generation
5. Image editing
6. Video generation
7. Voice messages
8. Voice calls
9. Memory controls
10. Message regeneration
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of the 10 features included.
evidence.helpText: Tick features you get without paying extra.

evidence.name: Included Credits
evidence.publicDescription: credits or tokens included in the subscription
evidence.internalInstructions: Record the exact credits or tokens included in the selected subscription.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of credits per billing period.
evidence.helpText: Tokens/credits included with a normal subscription.

evidence.name: Plan Limits
evidence.internalInstructions:
Record the exact daily or monthly limits for:
* Messages
* Images
* Videos
* Voice messages
* Voice calls
* Created characters
evidence.resultFormat: Exact limit for each feature or Unknown.
evidence.helpText: Daily/monthly caps on messages, images, etc.

evidence.name: Annual Discount
evidence.publicDescription: savings vs paying monthly for 12 months
evidence.internalInstructions:
Compare the annual plan total to 12× the monthly price on the same tier.
Record the percentage saved when paying annually.
evidence.resultFormat: Percentage discount on annual billing.

subscores.name: Usage Costs
subscores.description: Per-use costs for images, video, voice, calls, credit top-ups, and estimated monthly spend for regular use.

evidence.name: Voice Cost
evidence.publicDescription: estimated cost per 10 seconds of voice
evidence.internalInstructions:
Calculate how many credits one voice message costs.
Normalize to cost per 10 seconds using the duration configured in the Pricing tab.
evidence.resultFormat: Cost per 10 seconds of voice.
evidence.helpText: Cost per voice message or per minute.

evidence.name: Call Cost
evidence.publicDescription: estimated cost per voice call minute
evidence.internalInstructions:
Calculate how many credits one minute of voice calling costs.
Calculate the price using the cheapest credit package available to normal users.
evidence.resultFormat: Cost per voice call minute.

evidence.name: Top-Up Value
evidence.publicDescription: cheapest and most expensive credit packages
evidence.internalInstructions:
Record:
* Package price
* Included credits
* Cost per credit
Do this for the smallest and largest packages.
evidence.resultFormat: Smallest package, largest package and cost per credit.

evidence.name: Monthly Spend
evidence.publicDescription: estimated monthly cost for regular use
evidence.internalInstructions:
Calculate the full cost of the regular-use example:
* Required subscription
* 500 chat messages
* 20 images
* 4 videos
* 30 voice minutes
* Required credit top-ups
* Required payment fees
evidence.resultFormat: Estimated monthly cost for regular use.

subscores.name: Free Access
subscores.description: What users can do without paying: free chat, images, video, voice, characters, and free trial without credit card.

evidence.name: Free Chat
evidence.internalInstructions:
Record how many chat messages a free user can send before payment is required.
Include daily/monthly caps if they reset.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of free messages (e.g. 20 messages).

evidence.name: Free Images
evidence.internalInstructions: Record how many images a free user can generate before payment is required.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of free images (e.g. 3 images).

evidence.name: Free Video
evidence.internalInstructions: Record how many videos a free user can generate before payment is required.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of free videos (e.g. 1 video).

evidence.name: Free Voice
evidence.internalInstructions: Record how many seconds of voice messages or calls a free user gets before payment is required.
evidence.resultFormat: Free voice duration (e.g. 30 sec voice).

evidence.name: Free Characters
evidence.internalInstructions: Record how many characters a free user can create or chat with before payment is required.
evidence.resultFormat: Number of free characters (e.g. 1 character).

evidence.name: Free Value
evidence.publicDescription: overall free tier value and payment requirements
evidence.internalInstructions:
Record whether a meaningful free tier exists without a credit card.
Note: "No card needed", trial length, or card-required trial.
evidence.resultFormat: Short label (e.g. No card needed).

evidence.name: Restrictions
evidence.publicDescription: free access limits and reset rules
evidence.internalInstructions:
Record how free allowances reset or expire.
Examples: Resets daily, 7-day trial, credits expire after 30 days.
evidence.resultFormat: Short restriction label (e.g. Resets daily).

subscores.name: Billing
subscores.description: Pricing clarity, credit expiry, refunds, easy cancellation, and payment privacy (from Pricing tab).

evidence.name: Pricing Clarity
evidence.publicDescription: how clearly costs are explained before payment
evidence.internalInstructions:
Check whether the platform clearly shows these eight items before payment:
1. Subscription price
2. Renewal period
3. Included credits
4. Image cost
5. Video cost
6. Usage limits
7. Credit expiry
8. Refund policy
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of the eight pricing details clearly shown before payment.
evidence.shortDescription: Check which of the eight key pricing details are clearly shown before payment. The result is calculated automatically from the checks.
evidence.helpText: Tick what the site shows before checkout (price, limits, refunds, etc.).

evidence.name: Paywalls
evidence.publicDescription: core features behind an additional paywall
evidence.internalInstructions:
Check the same 10 core features used under Included Features.
Count how many require:
* A more expensive subscription
* Separate credits
* A separate purchase
evidence.resultFormat: Number and percentage of the 10 features behind an additional paywall.

evidence.name: Credit Expiry
evidence.internalInstructions: Check the pricing terms and account balance information.
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, No or Unknown, plus the expiry period.
evidence.helpText: Do bought credits expire? When?

evidence.name: Refunds
evidence.internalInstructions:
Review the refund policy.
Record:
* Whether refunds are allowed
* Refund request period
* Important restrictions
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited, No or Unknown.
evidence.helpText: Can you get money back? Any rules?

evidence.name: Cancellation
evidence.publicDescription: how easy it is to cancel a subscription
evidence.internalInstructions:
Try to cancel or locate cancellation instructions.
Record:
* Self-service cancellation available
* Steps required
* Whether support contact is needed
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited, No or Unknown.

evidence.name: Payment Privacy
evidence.internalInstructions:
Check checkout pages and payment help for:
* Discreet bank statement descriptor
* Whether billing name is shown before payment
* Privacy of payment method on statements
evidence.resultFormat: Yes, Limited, No or Unknown.
